To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 68000 is capable of achieving throughputs of 1-3 Mbits/s in the pattern recognition code, with a peak of 4 Mbits/s, and that it is possible to build a single board computer that is capable of achieving this throughput.

(1) The single board computer has the capability of performing pattern recognition on a large number of data sets in real time; (2) The single board can perform at least 20% of the pattern recognition required to analyze the raw data from the MPS II experiment; and, (3) The single board is a cost effective alternative to the CDC 76000 for performing pattern recognition on raw data sets from the ISABELLE experiments and other experiments that require similar pattern recognition capabilities.
